text:
Low carbohydrate intake can impair high-intensity exercise performance because the body relies on rapid glycolytic ATP production from carbohydrates, which fat oxidation cannot supply quickly enough. While this approach may offer benefits like weight loss or improved blood sugar control for some, it carries risks of fatigue and nutrient deficiencies if not carefully managed. Therefore, there is no universal benefit or harm without considering specific personal circumstances such as activity level and health status.
